title: Find the limit before the geometric stop
chapter: §6.3, §6.6 — effectiveness, usable authority and nonlinear limits
brief: Distinguish local effectiveness, usable travel, and nonlinear authority. This explicitly synthetic extension prevents a geometric stop from being mistaken for model validity.
supplied: Does a local slope establish the required ΔCm=-0.25 at a demanded 13.64° elevator deflection?
Local tangent ΔCm=-1.05*deltaDeg*pi/180. For this additional synthetic dataset, the documented local-fit interval is -10 to +10 deg; usable travel reaches +18 deg.
Synthetic extension of the chapter exercise: deltaDeg [-10,0,10,15,18]; observed ΔCm [0.183260,0,-0.183260,-0.20,-0.21]. These are teaching observations, not aircraft test data.
Local tangent estimate, supplied nonlinear observation, local-fit validity and authority conclusion.
The -1.05 per-radian slope is local. Reaching a travel stop does not establish flow attachment, actuator holding ability or rate capability.
At large positive deflection the local tangent overstates the magnitude in this synthetic dataset.
Linear estimate at 18°=-0.329867, but supplied synthetic response=-0.21, short of the -0.25 demand.
Check fit endpoints ±10°; 13.64° lies outside this local fit; maximum supplied negative response magnitude is only 0.21.
Label extrapolation separately from the supplied nonlinear observations; never present the geometric limit as a validated fit boundary.
Plot the tangent and the five supplied observations against deflection. Evaluate the requested deflection against the documented ±10° fit interval.
The local fit cannot establish the requested response; the supplied synthetic nonlinear screen is insufficient at the declared usable limit.

experience.scenario: The local elevator slope is qualified only from −10° to +10°. Usable travel reaches +18°, but the requested 13.64° lies outside the qualified fit. Synthetic nonlinear observations are supplied.
experience.task: Enter the fit limits and distinguish model qualification from available travel and from measured response sufficiency.
experience.method: A travel stop describes permitted motion; a fit interval describes where a model was qualified. Compare the local tangent with the supplied observations and the −0.25 demand. More negative response has larger negative-moment magnitude. No observation at 13.64° is supplied: the tangent there is an unqualified estimate.
experience.investigate: Inspect 10°, the requested 13.64°, and 18°. Record model qualification separately from the nonlinear evidence and demand.
experience.tools: Only this app and its calculation pad are needed.
